name: Puri
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; attested only in 19th-c. wordlists (e.g. Wied); no stress description exists.

new_statements.quote: Todo lo referido aquí en cuanto a la fonética y acentuación tiene por consiguiente un carácter hipotético. No es posible establecer una regla general para la acentuación en los idiomas de esta familia, parece probable que el acento tónico racae [sic] sobre la penúltima sílaba y en ciertos casos sobre la última. Resulta también muy difícil decidir si una vocal se [sic] breve o larga. Todos nuestros datos al respecto son dudosos.
new_statements.translation: Everything stated here about phonetics and accentuation is consequently hypothetical in character. It is not possible to establish a general rule for accentuation in the languages of this family; it seems probable that the tonic accent falls on the penultimate syllable and in certain cases on the last. It is also very difficult to decide whether a vowel is short or long. All our data in this respect are doubtful.
new_statements.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1937. La familia lingüística coroado. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 29(1): 157-214. doi:10.3406/jsa.1937.1952
new_statements.locator: p.162 (section 'Fonética', pp.161-162); PDF page 7; verified against page image
new_statements.rule_in_words: For the Puri-Coroado family as a whole (Coroado, Puri, Koropó), judged from accent marks in 19th-century wordlists: stress probably penultimate, with some words final-stressed; the author states no firm rule can be given and the whole account is hypothetical.
new_statements.exceptions: 'en ciertos casos sobre la última' — some words with final stress (consistent with Torrezão 1889's accent marks, e.g. nguê 'cabeça', kandú, chambé alongside tembóra, capôna).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms in old wordlists (Eschwege, Martius, Balbi, Noronha Torrezão for Puri); family-level generalisation, not Puri-specific; no phrase-level data; preceded (p.161) by the caveat that none of the vocabularies was recorded 'según las normas de la fonética moderna'.
new_statements.identity_note: Loukotka's statement is made for the whole 'familia coroado' (Coroado, Puri, Koropó) collectively, from philological analysis of 19th-c. wordlists (Puri sources P1-P4 = Eschwege, Martius, Balbi, Noronha Torrezão), not from fieldwork on Puri alone; he flags it as hypothetical. Glottolog treats Puri (puri1262) and Coroado (coro1249) as separate languages of the Puri-Coroado family; Métraux 1946 calls Puri 'a dialect of Coroado'. The modern 'Kwaytikindo' revitalised Puri (2020-) is a reconstructed variety and was not accessed.

sources.note: 'Fonética' section pp.161-162: vowel/consonant inventories for Coroado, Puri, Koropó from old wordlists; p.162: no general accent rule can be established for the family, but the tonic accent probably falls on the penultimate syllable and in certain cases on the last; all explicitly hypothetical.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens II: Wörtersammlung brasilianischer Sprachen / Glossaria linguarum brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. (Puri list pp.194-195)
sources.note: Puri wordlist pp.194-195 with some accent marks; only a general orthographic note (pp.29-30) that the acute serves 'den Vocal zu schärfen oder die Sylbe zu betonen'; nothing Puri-specific on stress placement.

sources.citation: Bentivoglio, Julio (org.). 2017. História dos povos indígenas no Espírito Santo, vol. 1: Os Puri. Vitória: Editora Milfontes. 116 pp. (includes Portuguese translation of Ehrenreich 1886)
sources.note: Historical/ethnographic volume; pp.84-86 reproduce Ehrenreich's sound key and wordlist in Portuguese; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ribeiro, Eduardo Rivail. 2009. Old data, new cognates: the case of the 'marker of alienable possession' in the Kamakã, Purí, and Krenák families. Cadernos de Etnolingüística, Série Notas 2: 1-5.
sources.note: Morphological note on a possession marker; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Silva Neto, Ambrósio Pereira da. 2007. Revisão da classificação da família lingüística Purí. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade de Brasília. ix+74 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 3.1.1 'Levantamento dos sons da língua Purí' (and 3.2.1 Coroado, 3.3.1 Koropó, 3.4 reconstruction) gives segment inventories by environment only; full-text search for acento/tônica/sílaba/prosódia finds nothing — silent on stress.

sources.citation: Métraux, Alfred. 1946. The Purí-Coroado linguistic family. In J. H. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 1: The Marginal Tribes, 523-530. Washington: Smithsonian (BAE Bulletin 143).
sources.note: Ethnographic; only says Puri is a dialect of Coroado and Koropó more distant; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Torrezão, Alberto de Noronha. 1889. Vocabulario Puri. Revista Trimensal do Instituto Historico e Geographico Brazileiro 52(1): 511-514.
sources.note: Wordlist (collected Abre-Campo 1885) with acute/circumflex accents marking tonic vowels (nguê, kandú, chambé, tembóra, katahra, capôna...), mix of final and penult; no rule stated, only ethnographic closing note.

sources.citation: Ehrenreich, Paul. 1886. Bemerkungen über die Puris Ostbrasiliens. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 18: 184-188.
sources.note: scanned (no text layer): a key of 'eigenthümliche Laute' (θ, guttural aspirate, å, r/l liquid, ng, y) and an accented wordlist (ariníng, penâng, tanguâ...); no statement on stress placement.
